lenses.label: Security
lenses.summary: Two layers keep a request flood and a bad caller from doing damage: a throttle at the front door and a least-privilege role on the function.

lenses.label: Cost
lenses.summary: Everything bills per use, so cost tracks traffic and idle time costs almost nothing.

detail.why: A static front end needs no server of its own.

security.text: No secrets ship in the bundle, so there is nothing to leak from the page.

cost.text: Static files on a CDN; hosting cost is negligible.

detail.role: Front door for all requests. Throttles before any code runs.
detail.why: A hard limit caps the cost of a request flood.

security.text: Throttling bounds the worst case of a flood, even if every other control failed.

cost.text: HTTP APIs bill per request with no idle charge; roughly $1 per million.

reliability.text: Runs across zones with no servers to patch or fail over.

risks.text: Buffering responses keeps the API simple and cheap but rules out token-by-token streaming.

detail.role: Validates input, reads and writes data.

security.text: The role allows only the one table and the one bucket it needs, nothing else.

cost.text: Billed per invocation and run time; effectively free at low traffic.

reliability.text: Failed invocations are retried automatically before an error is returned.

risks.text: Retries are safe because every write is conditional and idempotent.

detail.why: Scales to zero and needs no servers.

security.text: Data is encrypted at rest, and only the function's role can read or write it.

cost.text: On-demand billing: you pay per read and write, with nothing for idle capacity.

reliability.text: A region outage takes the database down; point-in-time restore only covers data loss.

risks.text: Single-region deployment: a regional outage stops the whole app.

security.text: The bucket is private with no public access; backups cannot be read by the web tier.

cost.text: Storage is billed per GB; a small app costs cents per month.

reliability.text: Backups live in the same region as the data they protect.

links.label: POST /items
links.detail: One HTTPS request per action, with a JSON body.

security.text: Every call is HTTPS and carries a signed token the API verifies.

cost.text: The request is the unit of billing at the API.

links.label: Invoke
links.detail: The API applies the throttle, then calls the function.

security.text: The API can invoke this one function and nothing else.

cost.text: No separate charge beyond the request and the invocation.

links.label: Read / write
links.detail: A single conditional write per request.

security.text: Calls are signed with the function's role; no passwords are stored.

cost.text: Each read or write unit is billed on demand.

links.label: Backup
links.detail: Nightly copy. Not on the request path.

security.text: The copy never leaves the account and is encrypted in transit.

cost.text: A small nightly copy costs cents per month.

trace.label: Request hits the throttled front door

prose.text: A browser calls an API, which runs a function that stores records in a database. Uploads and backups go to object storage.
